title: Federico Chaves Assumes Presidency
description: Federico Chaves of the Colorado Party assumed the Paraguayan presidency after a period of political instability, consolidating Colorado Party dominance that would last for over six decades. His government maintained the authoritarian tradition established by earlier regimes and relied heavily on the party's network of patronage. The Chaves presidency set the stage for the Stroessner coup five years later.

title: Stroessner Seizes Power in Military Coup
description: General Alfredo Stroessner overthrew President Federico Chaves on May 8, 1954, in a coup backed by the Colorado Party and the armed forces. Stroessner would go on to rule Paraguay for 35 years — the longest dictatorship in South American history. His regime combined extreme personal loyalty networks, political repression, and selective economic development.

title: Stroessner Elected President in Controlled Vote
description: Alfredo Stroessner was elected president in July 1954, running as the Colorado Party candidate after suppressing opposition. He would subsequently win seven consecutive fraudulent elections holding power until 1989. The elections became a ritualized legitimation mechanism for his authoritarian rule.

title: Colorado Party Purged; Stroessner Consolidates Control
description: Stroessner systematically purged rival factions within the Colorado Party, imprisoning or exiling internal opponents to consolidate his personal control over the state apparatus. Membership in the Colorado Party became a practical prerequisite for employment in the public sector. The party-state fusion became a defining feature of the stronismo regime.

title: Political Opposition Crushed; Exiles Flee to Argentina
description: The Stroessner regime intensified repression against Liberal Party politicians, trade unionists, and dissidents, forcing thousands into exile primarily in Argentina. The secret police, known as the Pyrague (informants), penetrated civil society extensively. Paraguay's political exile community in Buenos Aires became a significant opposition force in absentia.

title: Concepción Uprising Suppressed
description: Armed opposition groups linked to the Febrerista Party and exiled Liberals launched an armed incursion from Argentina that was swiftly crushed by Paraguayan security forces. The failed insurgency prompted further waves of arrests and tightened border controls. Stroessner used the episode to justify extending emergency powers.

title: Paraguay Joins Alliance for Progress
description: Paraguay joined the US-led Alliance for Progress, receiving development aid linked to Cold War containment strategy in Latin America. The Kennedy administration viewed Stroessner's anti-communism as sufficient grounds for partnership despite his authoritarian rule. Aid funded infrastructure and agricultural projects but reinforced the regime's stability.

title: State of Siege Normalized; Routine Renewals Begin
description: Stroessner placed Paraguay under a continuous state of siege that was routinely renewed by the subservient parliament every 90 days, suspending constitutional rights indefinitely. The legal mechanism allowed arbitrary detention without judicial review and silenced press freedom. This normalized emergency rule became a hallmark of the regime.

title: Itaipú Dam Negotiations Begin with Brazil
description: Paraguay and Brazil began formal discussions over joint hydroelectric development of the Paraná River, eventually leading to the 1973 Treaty of Itaipú. The project would reshape Paraguay's economy and create deep Brazilian economic influence. Stroessner used the prospective revenues to strengthen political loyalty networks.

title: New Stroessner Constitution Enacted
description: Paraguay adopted a new constitution that formalized Stroessner's authoritarian system, permitting indefinite presidential re-election and concentrating power in the executive. The document included nominal rights guarantees that were routinely ignored in practice. It replaced the 1940 constitution and provided a legal veneer for continued one-man rule.

title: Operation Condor Precursor: Repression Networks with Argentina and Brazil
description: Paraguay deepened intelligence-sharing arrangements with Argentina and Brazil to track and eliminate leftist exiles, anticipating the formal Operation Condor network established in 1975. Paraguayan security forces cooperated with DINA and SIDE in extrajudicial cross-border operations. This coordination resulted in forced disappearances of political opponents across the Southern Cone.

title: Treaty of Itaipú Signed with Brazil
description: Paraguay and Brazil signed the Treaty of Itaipú on April 26, 1973, establishing the framework for the binational Itaipú hydroelectric dam on the Paraná River. Critics noted that the treaty's terms were heavily favorable to Brazil, setting the energy price at a fixed low rate. The dam would eventually become the world's largest hydroelectric power station by output.

title: Paraguay Joins Operation Condor
description: Paraguay officially joined Operation Condor, the US-backed South American intelligence network coordinating the kidnapping, torture, and murder of political dissidents across national borders. The Paraguayan secret police, under Pastor Coronel, was a key participant. Thousands of Paraguayan and regional exiles would be targeted through this network.

title: Itaipú Dam Construction Nears Completion; Economic Boom
description: Construction of the Itaipú Dam generated a short-lived economic boom with thousands of construction jobs and massive infrastructure investment along the Paraná River corridor. Ciudad del Este (then Puerto Presidente Stroessner) grew rapidly into a major commercial hub. The economic upswing temporarily boosted regime legitimacy.

title: Anastasio Somoza Takes Refuge in Paraguay
description: Nicaraguan dictator Anastasio Somoza Debayle, ousted by the Sandinista revolution, was granted asylum by Stroessner and settled in Asunción. His presence underscored Paraguay's status as a refuge for right-wing authoritarian leaders. Somoza was assassinated in Asunción in September 1980 in a Sandinista-linked operation.

title: Itaipú Dam Inaugurated
description: The Itaipú Dam was inaugurated on October 25, 1982 after years of construction, becoming the largest hydroelectric project in the world at that time by installed capacity. Paraguay immediately became one of the world's largest per-capita producers of electricity, though most of its share was sold to Brazil at below-market rates. The dam transformed Paraguay's economic geography but the terms of the treaty remained controversial.

title: Post-Itaipú Economic Recession Sets In
description: With construction on Itaipú complete, Paraguay entered a sharp economic recession as tens of thousands of construction workers lost employment and foreign investment dried up. The drop in GDP exposed the structural fragility of a boom built on one mega-project. The recession fueled social discontent that the regime struggled to contain.

title: ABC Color Newspaper Shut Down
description: The Stroessner regime closed the independent daily newspaper ABC Color, which had been the only significant critical voice in Paraguay's restricted press landscape. The closure deprived civil society of an important information outlet and silenced investigative reporting on corruption. The paper remained closed until after the 1989 coup.

title: Peasant Organizations and Land Conflicts Escalate
description: Rural tensions mounted as landless peasants organized under the National Coordinator of Peasant Organizations (MCNOC) pressed for land reform, clashing with the Colorado Party's land distribution patronage system. Large-scale soy farming expansion by Brazilian-owned farms displaced Paraguayan subsistence farmers. The agrarian conflict laid groundwork for social unrest that would persist beyond the dictatorship.

title: Catholic Church Increases Opposition to Stroessner
description: The Paraguayan Catholic Church, under Bishop Aníbal Maricevich and influenced by liberation theology, intensified its criticism of the Stroessner regime's human rights abuses and corruption. Church radio stations became key channels for independent information. The church's stance gave moral authority to opposition movements and alienated traditional Catholic support from the regime.

title: Stroessner Re-elected for Eighth Term Amid Splits
description: Alfredo Stroessner won his eighth presidential election in February 1988 under heavily controlled conditions, but internal Colorado Party tensions between the 'militants' and 'traditionalists' were reaching a breaking point. The elderly Stroessner's declining health and the question of succession fueled factional conflict. The election would prove to be his last.

title: Coup Ousts Stroessner; End of 35-Year Dictatorship
description: General Andrés Rodríguez, Stroessner's son-in-law and army commander, overthrew the aging dictator on February 3, 1989 in a military coup. Stroessner fled to Brazil where he died in exile in 2006. The coup ended 35 years of dictatorship — the longest in South American history — and initiated a transition toward constitutional democracy.

title: Rodríguez Wins Transitional Election; ABC Color Reopens
description: General Andrés Rodríguez won the presidential election of May 1989 with over 74% of the vote, continuing Colorado Party rule under a nominally democratic framework. The previously closed newspaper ABC Color was permitted to reopen, marking a significant step toward press freedom. International observers noted the election's organizational shortcomings but accepted the transition.

title: Terror Archive (Archive of Terror) Located
description: Paraguayan police in 1992 discovered thousands of files documenting Operation Condor's crimes across the Southern Cone, known as the Archive of Terror, in a police precinct in Asunción. The discovery provided crucial evidence of systematic human rights violations under Stroessner and linked Paraguay to cross-border state terrorism. The archive became a landmark resource for human rights accountability in Latin America.

title: New Democratic Constitution Adopted
description: Paraguay adopted a new democratic constitution on June 20, 1992, prohibiting immediate presidential re-election, establishing an independent judiciary, and enshrining civil liberties. The constitution was a foundational document of Paraguay's democratic transition and brought a formal end to the legal architecture of stronismo. It remains in force today.

title: Juan Carlos Wasmosy Wins First Free Presidential Election
description: Juan Carlos Wasmosy won the 1993 presidential election in what observers considered Paraguay's first genuinely competitive democratic election, defeating Domingo Laíno of the Liberal Party. Wasmosy, a Colorado Party candidate, received 40% of the vote in a three-way race. The transfer of power from the military-Colorado apparatus to a civilian Colorado president was a meaningful democratic milestone.

title: Paraguay Joins MERCOSUR
description: Paraguay became a full member of the Southern Common Market (MERCOSUR) alongside Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay when the bloc came into force in January 1995 under the Treaty of Ouro Preto. Trade integration boosted Paraguay's soy and cattle exports. Membership also created obligations around democratic governance that would later be invoked during the 2012 suspension.

title: General Oviedo Attempted Coup Against Wasmosy
description: Army commander General Lino Oviedo attempted a coup against President Wasmosy in April 1996, demanding the president's resignation before ultimately backing down under US pressure and threats of regional isolation. Wasmosy resisted the ultimatum and Oviedo was eventually arrested and convicted. The episode demonstrated the fragility of Paraguay's democratic institutions and the military's continued political ambitions.

title: Cubas Grau Elected; Pardons Oviedo
description: Raúl Cubas Grau, a close Oviedo ally, won the 1998 presidential election and almost immediately pardoned Oviedo from his prison sentence, directly defying a Supreme Court ruling ordering the conviction upheld. The pardoning created an immediate constitutional crisis and united opposition parties and civil society against the new government. The OAS and international community condemned the move.

title: Vice President Argaña Assassinated; March Crisis
description: Vice President Luis María Argaña was assassinated on March 23, 1999 in a brazen daylight attack in Asunción, widely attributed to Oviedo's faction. The murder triggered massive protests known as the Marzo Paraguayo, during which eight young demonstrators were shot dead by snipers linked to the government. President Cubas Grau resigned and fled to Brazil, Oviedo fled to Argentina, and Senate president Luis González Macchi assumed the presidency.

title: González Macchi Assumes Presidency After Resignation Crisis
description: Senate president Luis González Macchi was constitutionally elevated to the presidency in late March 1999 following the resignation of Cubas Grau. His government was marked by severe economic mismanagement, corruption scandals, and a banking crisis. González Macchi became the first Paraguayan president to face an impeachment attempt (which failed in 2003).

title: Failed Coup Attempt by Oviedo Supporters
description: Soldiers loyal to exiled General Lino Oviedo launched a brief coup attempt in May 2000, seizing the army headquarters in Asunción before government forces regained control within hours. The failed putsch further destabilized González Macchi's already embattled government. Paraguay formally requested Oviedo's extradition from Argentina.

title: Banking Crisis and Economic Collapse
description: Paraguay experienced a severe banking crisis with the failure of several major financial institutions amid revelations of massive fraud, depleting central bank reserves and shaking confidence in the financial system. The crisis coincided with Argentina's 2001–2002 economic collapse which severely reduced remittances and trade. GDP contracted sharply and poverty rates surged to over 40%.

title: Mass Protests Against González Macchi Government
description: Large-scale street protests erupted across Paraguay as unions, peasant organizations, and the political opposition demanded the resignation of President González Macchi over corruption, economic mismanagement, and the banking crisis. General strikes shut down large sections of the economy. The protests marked the emergence of a more assertive civil society in post-Stroessner Paraguay.

title: Nicanor Duarte Frutos Elected President
description: Nicanor Duarte Frutos won the presidential election for the Colorado Party in April 2003 with 37% of the vote, defeating candidates from the Liberal and Patria Querida parties. Duarte Frutos promised anti-corruption reforms and fiscal discipline, eventually engaging the IMF to restore macroeconomic stability. His term saw a modest economic recovery driven by soy prices.

title: EPP Guerrilla Group Emerges
description: The Ejército del Pueblo Paraguayo (EPP), a small Maoist-inspired guerrilla organization, carried out its first notable operations in the remote northern Concepción department. The EPP would engage in kidnappings, assassinations of security forces, and extortion throughout the following two decades. Despite its small size, the group became a persistent security challenge requiring sustained military operations.

title: Paraguay Extradites Lino Oviedo; Trial Begins
description: General Lino Oviedo, after periods of exile in Argentina and Brazil, was extradited to Paraguay and began facing trial for his role in the 1999 political crisis and assassination of Vice President Argaña. His legal travails would continue for years. Oviedo was later killed in a helicopter crash in 2013 shortly after his release from prison.

title: Alfredo Stroessner Dies in Brazilian Exile
description: Alfredo Stroessner, Paraguay's former dictator, died in Brasilia on August 16, 2006 at the age of 93 without ever facing trial for human rights abuses committed during his 35-year rule. His death without accountability reflected the incomplete nature of Paraguay's transitional justice process. Victims' groups renewed calls for reparations and historical recognition.

title: Duarte Frutos Reelection Bid Blocked; Term Limit Upheld
description: President Nicanor Duarte Frutos sought to change the constitution to allow his immediate re-election, but the Supreme Court blocked the attempt. The ruling reinforced the 1992 constitution's single-term limit for presidents. The episode demonstrated both the continuing temptation of executive power consolidation and the relative resilience of Paraguay's constitutional guardrails.

title: Fernando Lugo Wins Presidential Election, Breaking 61 Years of Colorado Rule
description: Catholic bishop Fernando Lugo, running for the Patriotic Alliance for Change coalition, defeated the Colorado Party candidate Blanca Ovelar in the April 2008 presidential election, ending 61 consecutive years of Colorado Party control of the presidency. The election was widely seen as a historic democratic breakthrough for Paraguay. Lugo's victory was the first peaceful transfer of power to an opposition party in Paraguayan history.

title: Paraguay and Taiwan Relations Reaffirmed Under Lugo
description: Despite pressure from China, President Fernando Lugo confirmed that Paraguay would maintain its diplomatic recognition of the Republic of China (Taiwan), making Paraguay one of Taiwan's last remaining formal allies. Taiwan provides significant aid and investment in exchange for the relationship. The decision preserved a foreign policy continuity across the historic Colorado-to-opposition power shift.

title: Lugo Land Reform Stalls Amid Colorado Opposition
description: President Lugo's promised land redistribution program stalled in the face of a hostile Colorado-dominated legislature and powerful agricultural interests. Paraguay had one of the most unequal land distributions in the world, with 2% of landowners controlling 77% of agricultural land. The failure to deliver agrarian reform weakened Lugo's political base among peasant communities.

title: Ñacunday Land Conflict Intensifies
description: Tensions over land occupation in the Ñacunday district escalated into a major confrontation between Brazilian-owned soy farms and landless Paraguayan peasants who demanded redistribution. The conflict exposed the structural contradiction between agribusiness expansion and rural poverty. The episode was a precursor to the Curuguaty crisis two years later.

title: Paraguay Suspends from UNASUR Meeting Over EPP Crisis
description: The Lugo government declared a state of emergency in three northern departments in response to EPP guerrilla activity, deploying military units in a joint operation with police. The EPP's kidnapping of a cattle rancher drew international attention to the low-intensity conflict. The security operation became a recurring feature of Paraguayan politics through the 2020s.

title: Lugo Paternity Scandal and Political Weakening
description: President Lugo acknowledged fathering children with multiple women during his time as a Catholic bishop, triggering a national scandal and undermining his moral authority as a former clergyman. The revelation strengthened his political opponents within the coalition and in the legislature. Lugo's political isolation deepened, leaving him vulnerable to the legislative maneuver that would oust him.

title: Curuguaty Massacre: 17 Killed in Land Eviction
description: On June 15, 2012, a police operation to evict landless peasants from the disputed Marina Cue estate in Curuguaty turned violent, leaving 11 peasants and 6 police officers dead in a confrontation that shocked the nation. The circumstances of the massacre remained contested, with human rights groups questioning the official account. The episode was immediately exploited by Lugo's opponents as grounds for impeachment.

title: Lugo Impeached in 'Parliamentary Coup'
description: The Paraguayan Congress voted to impeach President Fernando Lugo on June 22, 2012, just days after the Curuguaty massacre, giving him less than 24 hours to prepare a defense and removing him from office within hours of the trial. Vice President Federico Franco assumed the presidency. MERCOSUR and UNASUR suspended Paraguay, with regional governments and many international observers condemning the process as a democratic rupture.

title: MERCOSUR Suspends Paraguay; Venezuela Admitted
description: Following the impeachment of President Lugo, MERCOSUR suspended Paraguay from the bloc's decision-making bodies under its democratic clause. With Paraguay absent, the remaining members used the opportunity to admit Venezuela — a move Paraguay had previously blocked. Paraguay's suspension lasted until after the 2013 elections.

title: Horacio Cartes Wins Presidential Election; Colorado Returns
description: Tobacco magnate and Colorado Party candidate Horacio Cartes won the presidential election in April 2013 with 46% of the vote, returning the Colorado Party to the presidency. His business background and promises of modernization attracted investor interest. Paraguay's suspension from MERCOSUR was lifted following the democratic election.

title: General Lino Oviedo Killed in Helicopter Crash
description: Former General Lino Oviedo, one of Paraguay's most destabilizing political figures of the democratic era, was killed in a helicopter crash in February 2013 shortly after his release from prison. His death removed a persistent source of political turbulence that had shaped Paraguayan politics since the 1990s. The circumstances of the crash were deemed accidental.

title: Soy and Beef Boom Drives Economic Growth
description: Paraguay experienced robust GDP growth driven by record soy and beef exports, benefiting from high global commodity prices and expanded cultivated area. The country became one of the world's top exporters of soy and a major beef exporter. The agribusiness boom widened inequalities and deepened environmental pressures but produced strong macroeconomic indicators.

title: Deforestation Crisis: Atlantic Forest Critically Threatened
description: Paraguay's Upper Paraná Atlantic Forest, one of the most biodiverse ecosystems in the world, reached critical fragmentation levels as soy expansion and cattle ranching continued to drive deforestation at among the highest rates in the world relative to forest cover. Environmental NGOs reported that less than 7% of Paraguay's original forest cover remained. The Zero Deforestation Law for the Eastern Region remained poorly enforced.

title: Senate Reelection Amendment Protests Turn Violent
description: The Paraguayan Senate approved a constitutional amendment that would allow President Horacio Cartes to seek a second consecutive term in a session held at midnight in June 2017, circumventing normal procedures. Outraged protesters stormed and set fire to part of the Congress building, with police using live ammunition against demonstrators. The violent crackdown killed one person and injured dozens, drawing international condemnation.

title: Reelection Amendment Ultimately Blocked
description: Following the violent protests and widespread domestic and international condemnation, the Cartes government abandoned the reelection constitutional amendment that had passed the Senate. The Supreme Court also signaled it would not validate the procedurally irregular vote. The episode marked a significant moment of civil society resistance to executive overreach in post-Stroessner Paraguay.

title: Mario Abdo Benítez Elected President
description: Mario Abdo Benítez, son of Stroessner's personal secretary and Colorado Party candidate, won the presidential election in April 2018 with 47% of the vote over opposition candidate Efraín Alegre. Abdo Benítez's election continued Colorado Party dominance but also raised concerns given his family's intimate connections to the Stroessner dictatorship. He took office pledging continuity of macroeconomic stability.

title: Itaipú Energy Deal Scandal and Near-Impeachment
description: A secret energy deal negotiated by the Abdo Benítez administration with Brazil over Itaipú's electricity terms was leaked, showing Paraguay agreed to pay far less than it was entitled to under a more favorable renegotiation. The scandal triggered impeachment proceedings in the Chamber of Deputies that Abdo narrowly survived. The affair highlighted the ongoing importance and domestic political sensitivity of the Itaipú treaty.

title: Paraguay Breaks Diplomatic Ties with Venezuela
description: Paraguay severed diplomatic relations with Venezuela in August 2019, citing the Maduro government's authoritarian turn and its recognition of Nicolás Maduro over the Lima Group's recognition of Juan Guaidó. The move aligned Paraguay with the US-backed regional coalition pressing for democratic change in Venezuela. The break also reflected Paraguay's broader alignment with conservative regional politics.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Hits Paraguay
description: Paraguay confirmed its first COVID-19 cases in March 2020 and imposed one of Latin America's earliest lockdowns, which initially contained the spread. The health system, chronically underfunded, faced severe strain as cases surged in subsequent waves. The pandemic exposed structural weaknesses in public health infrastructure and triggered significant economic contraction.

title: COVID-19 Vaccine Protests; Health System Collapse Fears
description: In March 2021, mass protests erupted across Asunción and other Paraguayan cities over the government's slow COVID-19 vaccine procurement and the near-collapse of the health system, with hospitals overwhelmed and patients dying outside emergency rooms. Protesters called for the resignation of the health minister and President Abdo Benítez. The unrest was among the most significant in Paraguay since the 2017 Congress fire.

title: US Treasury Sanctions Cartes and Friedmann for Corruption
description: The US Treasury Department imposed sanctions on former President Horacio Cartes and Allied Holdings founder Juan Ángel Friedmann under the Magnitsky Act, citing involvement in drug trafficking, corruption, and connections to Hezbollah's financial networks. The move was deeply embarrassing for Paraguay's political class and signaled serious US concern about state capture by criminal interests. Cartes, who remained a dominant force in the Colorado Party, denied all allegations.

title: Drought and Low Paraná River Levels Hit Economy
description: An exceptional drought caused the Paraná River to drop to historically low levels, severely curtailing Itaipú's electricity generation and disrupting inland river shipping that carries Paraguay's soy exports. The water crisis forced energy rationing and added hundreds of millions of dollars in economic losses. The event underscored Paraguay's structural vulnerability to climate variability.

title: Santiago Peña Elected President; Cartes Faction Wins
description: Colorado Party candidate Santiago Peña, closely associated with the Cartes faction, won the presidential election on April 30, 2023 with 43% of the vote, defeating the Liberal-led Concertación opposition coalition. The election was notable for US sanctions hanging over Cartes, whose organization funded Peña's campaign. International observers noted the election was technically free but raised concerns about undue influence.

title: Paraguay Reaffirms Taiwan Recognition Under Peña
description: Newly elected President Santiago Peña confirmed Paraguay's continued diplomatic recognition of Taiwan, rebuffing Chinese pressure to switch allegiances in exchange for economic benefits. Taiwan responded with pledges of additional investment and development assistance. Paraguay remained the only South American country and one of 12 worldwide to maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taipei.

title: Itaipú Treaty Renegotiation Begins with Brazil
description: The 1973 Itaipú Treaty's Annex C, which set the terms for the sale of Paraguay's unused electricity share to Brazil, was due for renegotiation as of 2023. Paraguay pressed for a significantly higher price for its energy, arguing the original terms were exploitative. Negotiations with Brazil became a major political issue with significant economic stakes — Itaipú accounts for a large share of Paraguay's state revenues.

title: EPP Activity Continues in Northern Paraguay
description: The Ejército del Pueblo Paraguayo continued its insurgent activity in the Concepción and Amambay departments, killing several soldiers and police officers in ambushes and carrying out extortion of landowners. The government maintained a joint military-police task force, the Fuerza de Tarea Conjunta, in a prolonged low-intensity counterinsurgency operation. Concerns grew about narco-trafficking networks intersecting with the EPP.

title: Itaipú Renegotiation Agreement Reached with Brazil
description: Paraguay and Brazil reached a landmark renegotiation of the Itaipú treaty's financial terms, with Brazil agreeing to substantially increase the price it pays for Paraguay's electricity share — a major diplomatic and economic victory for Asunción. The new terms would significantly boost Paraguay's royalty revenues from the dam. The agreement was hailed domestically as correcting 50 years of unfavorable terms.

title: Anti-Corruption Prosecutors Persecuted; Rule-of-Law Concerns
description: Several Paraguayan prosecutors and judges known for pursuing corruption cases against politically connected individuals faced disciplinary proceedings, forced transfers, or intimidation in 2024, raising alarm among civil society groups and international organizations. The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights and Transparency International documented a systematic pattern of judicial harassment. The cases underscored the fragility of institutional independence in Paraguay's democracy.

title: Deforestation in the Chaco Reaches Critical Levels
description: Satellite data confirmed that the Paraguayan Chaco, one of the last large dry forests in South America, continued to lose forest cover at rates among the highest in the world, driven by beef cattle ranching for export. Paraguay was identified as having one of the top five highest deforestation rates globally by area in 2023–2024. The environmental impact threatened biodiversity and accelerated regional climate feedback loops.
